overview:
**High fire danger continues today, driven by very dry fuels (ERC 80%) and low afternoon humidity (18%, exceeding the local threshold).**
- Danger climbs to Very High by Friday, Aug. 21, as ERC rises to 91% before easing back to High through the weekend.
- Winds stay light from the NE (7 mph) with no rain expected until late week, keeping fuels critically dry.
- Only 1 of 7 local watchout thresholds is met today (minimum relative humidity); no Red Flag Warning is currently posted for this area.
- Gunnison County remains in Stage 2 Fire Restrictions as of Friday, August 15th, banning open fires and campfires; check municipal and BLM rules for Ouray, Montrose, and other local counties.
- Nearby: the Gold Mountain Fire is burning in southwest Colorado, originating just two miles north of the City of Ouray, now roughly 39,700 acres and about 87% contained; the Elk Fire near Lake City (Hinsdale/Gunnison area) is about 7,400 acres and 35% contained.
